questions.prompt: What does iron need in order to rust? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Rusting needs both oxygen and water. Salt speeds it up, but sunlight and heat are not needed.
Rust (iron oxide) is a new substance with different properties.

questions.prompt: Match each object to the best way of preventing rust.
questions.explain: Moving parts are greased; large surfaces painted; sheets and pipes galvanised; utensils made from rust-proof alloys.

questions.prompt: In the Rust Race, why is the water in tube B boiled and covered with oil?
options: To remove dissolved air and stop more air getting in
To stop the nail from floating
questions.explain: Boiling drives out dissolved air; the oil layer stops air from dissolving back in. This tests water without oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which two tubes should you compare to find out whether WATER is needed for rusting?
options: Boiled water + oil (B) and galvanised nail (F)
questions.hint: Choose two tubes that differ ONLY in whether water is present.
questions.explain: A and C both have air; only C has water. That isolates water as the variable.

questions.prompt: Why do iron objects rust faster in coastal cities like Mumbai?
options: The air is humid and contains salt
questions.explain: More moisture and salt in the air both speed up rusting.

questions.text: Coating iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting is called ___.
questions.explain: Galvanisation: zinc protects the iron even when scratched.

questions.prompt: Sort the tubes: did the nail rust?
questions.explain: Only nails exposed to both air and water (and unprotected) rusted.

questions.prompt: A galvanised bucket gets a deep scratch that exposes the iron. Why does the iron still not rust quickly?
options: Zinc is more reactive, so it corrodes first and protects the iron
Iron cannot rust once it is in a bucket
questions.explain: Zinc reacts in preference to iron (sacrificial protection), so the iron is protected even at the scratch.

questions.prompt: Stainless steel doesn't rust. Give TWO reasons why we don't make every iron object (like bridges and gates) from stainless steel.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Stainless steel is much more expensive than ordinary iron or steel, so huge structures would cost far more. 2) It needs extra metals like chromium and nickel, which are limited resources that must be mined, so cheaper methods like painting or galvanising are often good enough.
rubric: I gave a second reason (resources, mining, other methods are good enough)
questions.explain: Choosing materials means balancing cost, resources and performance: a Criterion D skill.
